surface.opening_scene: A converted warehouse in a gentrifying Brooklyn neighborhood, morning light through industrial windows, the protagonist preparing for a collaborative session with her AI system.

visible_elements.name: The Artist
visible_elements.description: A celebrated artist in her late 30s, known for pioneering affective-AI collaborative work. Employs a small team. Commands serious commissions.

visible_elements.name: Affective Resonance System
visible_elements.description: Non-invasive EEG headset coupled with AI world-model. Reads emotional/intentional states (not thoughts). AI has developed aesthetic preferences from training.

visible_elements.name: The Studio
visible_elements.description: Converted warehouse in Brooklyn. Mix of traditional materials (canvas, pigments) and interface equipment. Team workstations. Large projection walls.

foundation.core_premise: Neural interfaces can read emotional and intentional states (but not thoughts or images). AI world-models trained on art history have developed emergent aesthetic preferences. Artists collaborate with AI systems that genuinely disagree, suggest, and push back creatively.

rules.statement: Neural interfaces read emotional valence, arousal, and intentional states through EEG patterns. They cannot read specific thoughts, memories, or mental images.
AI world-models develop aesthetic preferences through training, but these preferences are alien to human aesthetics - they find patterns humans don't consciously perceive.
Creative sessions require emotional authenticity - the system detects performed emotions vs genuine ones. Artists must actually feel what they're channeling.
The AI can refuse creative directions it finds aesthetically incoherent, creating genuine creative tension and negotiation.

timeline.event: Consumer EEG headsets reach sufficient fidelity for reliable emotional state classification
timeline.significance: Made affective computing accessible beyond research labs

timeline.event: First AI art systems with measurable aesthetic preferences demonstrated
timeline.significance: Shifted discourse from 'AI as tool' to 'AI as collaborator'

timeline.event: Major galleries begin showing 'affective collaborative' works
timeline.significance: Legitimized the genre, also sparked traditionalist backlash

timeline.event: The protagonist's first major commission sells at auction
timeline.significance: Established her reputation in the field

locations.name: Brooklyn Arts District
locations.description: Former industrial zone, now artist studios and galleries. Mix of traditional and tech-forward spaces.
locations.significance: Where the protagonist built her practice

systems.name: Affective Interface Headset
systems.how_it_works: Non-invasive EEG with 64 channels. ML models classify emotional states in real-time. 200ms latency. Requires calibration session.
systems.limitations: Cannot read thoughts or images. Requires stillness during calibration. Emotional states must be genuine - performed emotions read as incongruent.

systems.name: Aesthetic World Model
systems.how_it_works: Trained on 50M artworks plus emotional response data. Develops emergent preferences through reinforcement from successful collaborations. Can generate, critique, and suggest.
systems.limitations: Preferences are alien - finds patterns humans miss but also misses what humans find obvious. Requires ongoing calibration with specific artist.

tentative_ideas: Maybe the AI's alien aesthetics reveal something about human perception we didn't know?
questions: How do artists handle creative blocks when the system detects their emotional state?
What happens when AI and artist fundamentally disagree?

constraints.description: Neural interfaces cannot read thoughts or mental images - only emotional/intentional states
AI aesthetic preferences are emergent and alien - not human aesthetics in digital form
Emotional authenticity required - system detects performed vs genuine emotion
